title: Talk it through (free)
content:
## What you'll get

Emergent agents can talk through your idea before writing a single line of code. This article shows when to discuss, how a discussion naturally turns into a build, and what does and doesn't draw down your credit balance.

---

## What draws down credits

Credits are deducted when the agent performs **work** - generating code, running tests, deploying to the cloud, or calling external APIs (see [How credits work](/how-credits-work)). The agent can also help you decide [which prompt window](/which-prompt-window-should-i-use) fits your project (Starter, Pro or Infinite) before you commit.

<Callout type="warning" title="Draft - needs review">
This article's premise is that a pure planning conversation is free / does not consume credits. That claim is NOT stated in the existing docs and needs product confirmation before publishing. If confirmed, restore the "planning is free" framing here.
</Callout>

<Callout type="tip" title="Ask before you build">
If you're unsure whether your idea needs a database, authentication, or external integrations, just ask. The agent will help you choose the right starting point.
</Callout>

---

## When to discuss vs. jump straight in

**Start with a discussion if:**

- You're not sure exactly what you want yet (explore options, compare approaches).
- You need to decide between Starter, Pro, or Infinite windows and want guidance on which capabilities you'll actually need.
- Your project involves integrations, scheduling, or third-party APIs and you want to understand what's possible before committing.
- You want the agent to sketch a rough plan or architecture before generating files.

**Jump straight to building if:**

- You have a clear, specific request: "Build a landing page with a hero section and email signup form."
- You've already chosen the right [prompt window](/which-prompt-window-should-i-use) and know your project won't need databases or APIs (Starter) or definitely will (Pro).
- You're iterating on an existing app and just need a quick feature add.

The agent adapts to whichever style you prefer. A short discussion often saves credits later by ensuring the agent scaffolds the right architecture from the start.

---

## How discussion turns into a build

The transition is seamless. Once you've talked through your idea and feel ready, just say:

> "Okay, let's build it."

or

> "Create the app we just discussed."

The agent will summarize the plan, confirm which prompt window you're using, and begin the [chat-to-deployment flow](/the-chat-to-deployment-flow). At that point, credits start counting as code is generated, tests run, and files are committed.

If you change your mind mid-build, you can pause and discuss adjustments. Credits are drawn down as the agent generates, tests and deploys code.

<Callout type="note" title="Maxx mode uses more credits">
When you enable **Maxx mode** (the toggle in the prompt bar), the agent plans more thoroughly and runs deeper validation. This produces higher-quality results but consumes 2-4× the credits of a standard prompt. Save Maxx for the final build, not the planning phase.
</Callout>

---

## If something looks wrong

If the agent seems to be generating code during a planning conversation when you only wanted to talk, just say:

> "Wait - I'm not ready to build yet. I just want to discuss options."

The agent will stop and switch back to advisory mode. Any credits already spent on partial generation can't be refunded, but you can continue the discussion freely and restart when you're ready.

description: Not sure yet? Discuss your idea with the agent before building - it costs nothing.
